title: Chanan the Wicked
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Rav Huna’s time, as in Bava Kamma 37a: he struck a certain man; the case came before Rav Huna, who said to Chanan, “Go, give him half a zuz.” He had a bad zuz that he could not exchange; he struck him again and gave him the whole zuz. There, at 115a, he stole a cloak and sold it; [the case] came before Rav Huna, and they said there: “Granted that he is notorious for wickedness, he is not notorious for theft.”

notes.text: The compressed אתא is represented as the case coming before Rav Huna without inventing which litigant arrived. Saved Davidson Bava Kamma 37a fully names Rav Huna and preserves the half-zuz/second-blow sequence; 115a preserves the wickedness/theft distinction.
